recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a bounded completion of the published FHIR-27886 decision; broader CodeableReference service/action mappings such as ServiceRequest.code, Appointment.serviceType, and Encounter.serviceType remain on code because they describe services rather than supplied products.
issue_request: FHIR-27886 was Published as Persuasive with Modification. It asked whether CodeableReference should apply to workflow Event.code; the accepted resolution kept Request/Event/Definition.code as the action/service concept and added a 0..1 CodeableReference product element to Request, Event, and Definition for supplied or manipulated products.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged implementation commit 0583fe1e3ff39c208fab14d6dad951c311c4fc8e added product to the Definition, Request, and Event pattern spreadsheets, added Definition.code, and updated workflow extension sources. Current source inspection showed product-like resource mappings remained on Request.code/Event.code in several resources, and DeviceDispense.device still had a duplicate Event.code mapping despite already mapping to Event.product.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps definition, event, and request as active logical models and keeps workflow pattern extension profiles active. Current pattern source already contains the product rows and code usage notes. Confluence FHIR Workflow minutes for 2020-07-13 record FHIR-27886 as persuasive with modification, and Zulip searches found no contrary discussion.
reconciliation: Changed MedicationAdministration.medication, MedicationDispense.medication, MedicationStatement.medication, Immunization.administeredProduct, and NutritionIntake.nutritionItem.nutritionProduct to map to Event.product; changed MedicationRequest.medication to map to Request.product; removed the stale duplicate Event.code mapping from DeviceDispense.device; and updated the corresponding mapping exception files.
